**Luc Richard Mbah a Moute** (/ˌbɑː ɑː ˈmuːteɪ/ *BAH ah MOO-tay*; born 9 September 1986) is a Cameroonian former professional [basketball](Basketball "Basketball") player. Mbah a Moute also played for the [Cameroon national team](Cameroon_men's_national_basketball_team "Cameroon men's national basketball team").

Mbah a Moute is currently a player agent for [Creative Artists Agency](Creative_Artists_Agency "Creative Artists Agency") (CAA).[[1]](Luc_Mbah_a_Moute#cite_note-1)

## College career

Mbah a Moute attended [Montverde Academy](Montverde_Academy "Montverde Academy") in Florida from 2001 to 2005, where he was coached by [Kevin Sutton](Kevin_Sutton "Kevin Sutton").[[2]](Luc_Mbah_a_Moute#cite_note-2) Soon, he would be Westwood-bound to play for [Ben Howland](Ben_Howland "Ben Howland") and [UCLA](UCLA_Bruins_men's_basketball "UCLA Bruins men's basketball").

As a freshman in 2005–06, Mbah a Moute led the Pac-10 Champion Bruins in rebounding. Mbah a Moute led or tied for the lead for the Bruins in rebounding in 27 regular-season games. In the NCAA tournament, Mbah a Moute scored the winning layup at the end of a comeback win over [Gonzaga](Gonzaga_University "Gonzaga University") in the Sweet 16. Mbah a Moute also posted 17 points, 9 rebounds, 2 steals, and 1 assist in a Final Four victory over [LSU](Louisiana_State_University "Louisiana State University"). He was named the [NBA's Most Improved Player](NBA_Most_Improved_Player_Award "NBA Most Improved Player Award") in 2019, becoming the first player to win an NBA title in the same season. The following year, Siakam lead Toronto to the second-best record in the league, earning All-NBA Second Team while being named a starter in his first NBA All-Star Game.
